subject.title: [Bug]: Slack reaction_added/reaction_removed events never delivered via Socket Mode (multi-account, v2026.3.24)

question: What live Slack diagnostic evidence should be required before a maintainer sponsors a code change for this reaction-specific Socket Mode delivery failure?
rationale: Source inspection shows multiple plausible boundaries, but the available issue evidence does not prove whether Slack/Bolt never emits the envelope, OpenClaw drops it at the account/team filter, or later authorization suppresses it.

options.title: Require live envelope proof
options.body: Ask for redacted current-main Socket Mode reaction envelopes, gateway trace logs, and `channels status --probe` output before choosing a fix shape.

options.title: Fold into broader Socket Mode triage
options.body: Treat this as part of the broader Slack Socket Mode delivery/liveness investigation only if that thread gains reaction-specific diagnostics.

options.title: Sponsor manual live repro
options.body: Have a maintainer or QA runner reproduce the five-account Slack setup and collect the first drop boundary directly.

recommendation.title: Require live envelope proof
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted current-main Socket Mode reaction envelopes, gateway trace logs, and `channels status --probe` output before choosing a fix shape.

likelyOwner.reason: The likely unresolved boundary includes the account/team mismatch filter introduced in the Slack Socket Mode area.
